subtype: Approach: changing the plan when exams come [Revision]
passage:
Afreen: Minakshi, you got the tablet for two days in a row this week and I'm not complaining. But I saw your face last night.
Minakshi: I wasn't going to say anything. I know you have exams.
Afreen: That's the thing. The plan doesn't fit any more. On my exam days, you should get more time.
Minakshi: Really?
Afreen: For two weeks, until my papers are done. You have it first every evening.
Minakshi: And then?
Afreen: Then it balances back, or we make a new plan. Deal?
Minakshi: Deal. Thanks, Afreen di.

qa.q: For how long did Afreen say Minakshi would get extra time?
qa.a: Afreen said for two weeks, until the papers are done.

qa.q: What did Afreen notice about Minakshi's face, and what might Minakshi have been feeling?
qa.a: Afreen noticed Minakshi's face the night before, which suggests Minakshi felt disappointed or left out, though Minakshi tried not to say so.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Afreen and Minakshi use, and why?
qa.a: They could set a fixed short time for Afreen to use the tablet after study, or ask a parent to help. Any plan should fit both children's needs.

qa.q: How does the new plan look to Minakshi?
qa.a: Minakshi asked 'Really?' and thanked Afreen, so Minakshi seems surprised and relieved that Afreen noticed and offered a fix.

grounding: When the older sibling has exams, the children notice the schedule is unfair, talk, and agree the younger gets more time for two weeks.

subtype: Approach: changing the plan when exams come [Revision]
passage: Last month my board-style mock exams started, and I realised our TV chart was not fair any more. Every evening, from six to seven, it was my hour, but I had to study, so the TV just sat there. And Payal, my little sister, had only her half hour. She kept looking at the dark screen. I felt a bit guilty. So I said, "Payal, for the next two weeks, you take my hour too." She squealed. "But when exams finish, I get extra, okay?" I said. She thought about it very seriously. "Okay, Rajni didi, two weeks for two weeks." We wrote it on the chart in pencil. Now exams are over, and it's my turn to catch up.

qa.q: Which hour was Rajni's time on the TV chart?
qa.a: Rajni's hour was from six to seven.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel seeing the TV sit unused while Payal looked at the dark screen?
qa.a: Rajni felt a bit guilty, seeing that the old plan had become unfair to Payal during exams.

qa.q: What else could the sisters do if another busy time comes up?
qa.a: They could agree that whoever is busy lends time and gets it back later, so the chart can bend without new fights.

qa.q: How does the exam-time change look to Payal?
qa.a: Payal is delighted, squealing at the extra time, and she takes the deal seriously enough to agree to pay it back.

grounding: It shows siblings noticing their schedule becomes unfair during exams and agreeing the younger gets more time for two weeks, to balance later.

subtype: Approach: changing the plan when exams come [Revision]
passage:
Note on the fridge, for Abbu to read when he gets home
I watched something nice today. Tanvir's final exams start Monday, and at lunch he said to Zoha, "You can take my computer hour for the next two weeks. I have to study anyway." Zoha looked shocked, then asked, "And after?" Tanvir said, "After, you give me back a few days. It'll balance." They sat together at the chart and changed two weeks of names in pencil. I didn't have to say a word. I've put a star on the chart and promised both of them a family film night when exams finish, so the trade feels like a win for both. Please praise them at dinner.
- Ammi (Vidya)

qa.q: When do Tanvir's final exams start?
How did Zoha feel when Tanvir offered his computer hour?
qa.a: Zoha looked shocked at first and then asked about afterwards, which suggests surprise and a careful kind of pleasure.

qa.q: What else could help keep the trade fair after exams?
qa.a: They could mark on the chart exactly which days Zoha gives back, so no one has to remember the deal.

qa.q: How does the trade look to Ammi?
qa.a: Ammi is pleased and proud, noting that she did not have to say a word, and adds a reward for both.

grounding: It shows siblings noticing a schedule would be unfair during exams and agreeing that the younger gets more time for two weeks, to balance later.
